summary: @or-sdk/apps ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime and executes a 727KB obfuscated blob
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style hex-named identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`,...) and control-flow flattening. On `npm install`, it downloads the Bun runtime (`bun-v1.3.13`) from GitHub, extracts and chmods the `bun` binary, then invokes `execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'], {cwd: D})` against an in-tarball 727KB Bun-compiled blob (`math_init.js`, header `// @bun @bun-cjs`). The blob is heavily packed with a rotated string-array cipher (`WV8StW` shift-decoder) and a custom base64-like alphabet, and no corresponding source is shipped in the tarball. The package's advertised purpose is a thin OneReach `getApps()` REST client, which requires no alternate runtime and no local script execution at install. Fetching a second language runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated, undocumented payload unrelated to the advertised SDK function is the canonical alternate-runtime-dropper shape, and executes at install time before the consumer sees any code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
